selectedDefects.issueTitle: API /commits returns incorrect X-Total-Count when using since/until filters (v1.25)
selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: fix(api): respect since/until when counting commits for X-Total-Count

contract.kind: OpenAPI 2 template committed in the repository and served by the running instance

selectedDefects.offlineStack: one pinned gitea image over SQLite with a repository seeded through the API; no third-party service
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the trigger is a single GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits?sha=main&since=...&until=... and the violation is entirely in the response: the body honours the filter while the X-Total-Count header reports the unfiltered repository-wide count. That is the backend-contract adapter's exact shape, one request and one response checked against the documented pagination contract, with the oracle computable from the response alone by comparing the header integer against the returned page when the page is not full. The fix touches only implementation code, so the contract text is unchanged across the pair
remaining: seed commits with pinned author timestamps so the filtered count is deterministic
stand the affected and fixed images up from source builds of both revisions and record the build commands
state the oracle as a header-versus-body invariant so it does not depend on a hardcoded expected number

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Repository `has_code` is always false when fetching a repository via the API

contract.kind: OpenAPI 2 template committed in the repository; has_code is a documented property of the Repository schema

selectedDefects.offlineStack: one pinned gitea image over SQLite with one repository created through the API
selectedDefects.whySuitable: a documented response field is never populated, so GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo} returns has_code false on a repository whose code unit is enabled. The oracle is a field-level comparison between two responses of the same service, the repository object and its unit configuration, so it needs no external knowledge and no state beyond one created repository. It is a different violation class from the pagination candidate, which keeps the two gitea candidates from collapsing into one identity
remaining: confirm the unit configuration is readable over the same API so the oracle stays self-contained
build both revisions and record the build commands

selectedDefects.issueTitle: REST API `POST`/`PATCH` request without a trailing slash causes an exception
selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: Fixes #21906: Return a 404 for REST API writes to endpoints with no trailing slash

contract.kind: OpenAPI 3 artifact committed in the repository

selectedDefects.offlineStack: the netbox image plus pinned Postgres and Redis images, seeded through the REST API
selectedDefects.whySuitable: a write to a path without its trailing slash raises an unhandled framework error, so the service answers a JSON-accepting API request with a 500 whose body is HTML. Both halves of that are contract violations, the status class and the content type, and both are visible in a single request and response pair with no state beyond one existing object. This is the clearest error-contract candidate in the pool and it belongs to a second, independent service
remaining: pin one object identifier through a seeded fixture so the request is reproducible
assert on content type and status class rather than on the error body text
build both revisions and record the build commands

selectedDefects.issueTitle: TokenViewSet.create() does not return v2 token plaintext
selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: Closes #22081: Include plaintext when creating v2 tokens via REST API

contract.kind: OpenAPI 3 artifact committed in the repository; the creation response documents the token value

selectedDefects.offlineStack: the netbox image plus pinned Postgres and Redis images
selectedDefects.whySuitable: POST to the token collection returns 201 with the documented token field null, because the view re-serializes from the database after creation and discards the write-only plaintext that exists only in memory. The oracle is a nullability check on one documented response field of one POST, which is the simplest possible conformance assertion, and it is a different violation class from the error-contract candidate on the same service
remaining: confirm the field is documented as non-null on the creation response at the affected revision rather than only implied by the changelog
build both revisions and record the build commands

selectedDefects.issueTitle: API call /admin/identities/{id}/credentials/{type} doesn't return expected statuscode and body
selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: fix: Return the updated identity as described in the API spec

contract.kind: OpenAPI artifact committed in the repository

selectedDefects.offlineStack: kratos over SQLite with the courier in development mode; the identity and its credential are created through the admin API
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the committed specification declares the credential-deletion operation as 200 with the updated identity in the body and the implementation answered 204 with no body. Status code and body presence are the two most primitive things the contract fixes, so this is the textbook conformance case for the target, and it comes from a third independent service
remaining: confirm the fix moved the implementation toward the spec rather than moving the spec, by diffing .schema/openapi.json across the revision pair
attach a TOTP credential through the admin API without a browser flow
build both revisions and record the build commands

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Getting public memos results in "authorization required"
selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: fix: allow public memo API access without authentication

contract.path: proto/api/v1 service definitions with proto/gen/openapi.yaml committed alongside
contract.kind: authored protobuf service definition plus a generated and committed OpenAPI artifact

selectedDefects.offlineStack: one memos container over SQLite with no external service at all
selectedDefects.whySuitable: one authenticated write seeds a memo with public visibility, then one anonymous GET must return it. The affected revision answers with an authorization error, which contradicts the security requirements the contract records for that operation. The trigger is two plain HTTP exchanges with no browser and no third party, and it is a fourth independent service, which is what gives this target a real margin
remaining: confirm the operation carries no security requirement in the committed contract at the affected revision
build both revisions and record the build commands

blockers.detail: no service in this record has been stood up and no request has been issued. Every revision pair, contract path, license and title here was verified against the GitHub API from the host; nothing has been executed

for none of the six candidates has the contract artifact been diffed across the revision pair, so it is not yet proven that each fix moved the implementation toward the committed contract rather than moving the contract toward the implementation. One further gitea candidate, pull request 38590 for issue 38581, was found and deliberately not selected precisely because it edits templates/swagger/v1_json.tmpl, which makes it a specification change rather than a conformance defect
